_about: Alkene addition rows (docs/ch8-10-app-gaps.md, 'Design: an addition engine that never guesses'). Checked in order, first match wins, like rules.json. when: sub (alkene | alkane), act (the reagent's `add` role in reagents.json), x (halogen of HX/X2), heat, light, peroxide, water. then: intermediate (cation | halonium | radical | concerted | surface | ozonide | none), regio (markovnikov | anti-markovnikov | none), stereo (syn | anti | none), shifts, adds { more, less } (what ends up on the more / less substituted C=C carbon), stereospecific (Y | N), build (markovnikov | radical | ozonolysis; missing = the product builder isn't written yet, so the row says addition_not_yet but still reports its classification), session (when the builder lands), template (viewer, S4), reasons. notCovered rows stop with that reason. Rows may carry tags: course | disagree.

reasons.not_sn_e_reagent: This isn’t an SN/E reagent (it has an O–O, X–X or H–H bond, or boron: an oxidant, halogen, H₂ or borane), so no SN/E role is estimated for it. If it’s in the reagent list, type its name instead.
reasons.addition_not_yet: This is an alkene: this addition (Ch 8) isn’t built yet, so no product is shown. The card still says what kind of addition it is.
reasons.radical_not_yet: This is an alkane with a halogen and light: radical halogenation (Ch 10) isn’t covered yet.
reasons.addition_alkene_type: A C=C carbon here carries O, N, a halogen, or is conjugated with C=O or C≡N. Those change where H⁺ adds, and the addition engine doesn’t cover them yet.
reasons.conjugated_diene: Conjugated diene: 1,2- vs 1,4-addition isn’t covered yet.
reasons.several_alkenes: This molecule has more than one C=C, and one equivalent of reagent could add to either. The app doesn’t pick one.
reasons.alkyne_not_covered: Additions to C≡C (alkynes) aren’t covered yet.
reasons.workup_alone: This is the second half of a two-part step (it follows BH₃ or O₃). Type both, e.g. “1) O₃ 2) DMS”.
reasons.needs_workup: BH₃ and O₃ are two-part steps: the first part alone gives an organoborane or an ozonide, which the course never stops at. Add the second part (BH₃ → H₂O₂/HO⁻; O₃ → DMS or Zn/HOAc).
reasons.needs_catalyst: H₂ alone doesn’t add to a C=C: it needs a metal catalyst (Pd/C, Pt, PtO₂ or Ni).
reasons.oxidative_workup: O₃ with an oxidative workup (H₂O₂) turns aldehydes into carboxylic acids. That isn’t covered yet; reductive workup (DMS or Zn/HOAc) is.
reasons.hydration_vs_dehydration: Acid with heat and no water on an alkene: hydration is an equilibrium, and heat without water pushes it back toward the alkene (dehydration). Add water (H₂SO₄ in H₂O) for hydration.
reasons.allylic_needs_nbs: Br₂/Cl₂ with an alkene still adds across the C=C, even with light. Substituting an allylic H needs NBS (low Br₂ concentration), which isn’t covered yet.
reasons.alkene_also_reacts: The C=C can also add this reagent; only the substitution/elimination at the leaving group is shown.
reasons.markovnikov: Markovnikov: H⁺ adds to the C=C carbon that leaves the more stable carbocation (more carbons on C⁺, or allylic/benzylic). The nucleophile then bonds to C⁺.
reasons.cation_shifts: A carbocation can rearrange: a 1,2-hydride or methyl shift happens only if it gives a more stable cation.
reasons.markovnikov_tie: Both ends of the C=C give equally stable carbocations, so both products form (competing). The app doesn’t pick one.
reasons.hydration: Acid-catalysed hydration: H⁺ adds (Markovnikov), water bonds to C⁺, then loses H⁺ to give the alcohol.
reasons.acid_water_assumed: Acid without heat on an alkene is read as hydration in water (the usual conditions), so OH ends up on the more substituted carbon.
reasons.hbr_radical: HBr with peroxides (ROOR) goes by a radical chain: Br• adds to the C=C end that leaves the more stable radical, so Br ends up on the less substituted carbon (anti-Markovnikov).
reasons.radical_no_shift: Radicals don’t do 1,2-shifts here, so there’s no rearrangement.
reasons.only_hbr_radical: Only HBr adds by the radical chain. With HCl or HI one step of the chain is uphill, so peroxides change nothing: it’s an ordinary Markovnikov addition.
reasons.halonium_no_shift: Br₂/Cl₂ form a three-membered bridged halonium ion: no free carbocation, so no shifts, and the nucleophile opens it from the back (anti).
reasons.halohydrin_regio: Water opens the halonium ion at the more substituted carbon, which carries more δ+.
reasons.concerted_no_shift: Concerted: all bonds form at once, there’s no intermediate, so nothing can rearrange.
reasons.hydroboration_regio: B goes to the less substituted carbon (less crowded); H₂O₂/HO⁻ then swaps B for OH with retention, so OH ends up on the less substituted carbon (anti-Markovnikov), syn with the new H.
reasons.hydrogenation_surface: H atoms are delivered from the metal surface to one face of the C=C (syn).
reasons.ozonolysis_cut: Ozonolysis cuts every C=C: each alkene carbon becomes a C=O. A ring C=C gives one chain with two carbonyls; =CH₂ leaves as formaldehyde.
reasons.reductive_workup: Reductive workup (DMS or Zn/HOAc) keeps aldehydes as aldehydes.
reasons.racemic_flat: The new stereocentre forms at a flat carbocation or radical, so both faces react equally: a racemic mixture (±).
reasons.mixture_flat: The new stereocentre forms at a flat carbocation or radical next to another stereocentre: a mixture of diastereomers.
